categories.desc: The “Jeez!” moments: a small frustration, nothing serious.
cards: A softened stand-in for a much ruder word. Very common, and fine among friends and family.
Another softened swear, just as mild as purée.
Gentle frustration, quieter than the others.
A Swiss-army knife: surprise, dismay or amazement. The tone does the work.
Oh là là, il y a du monde.
Wow, there are a lot of people.

categories.desc: Surprise, from pleasant to properly shocked.
cards: Ça alors ! Tu es déjà là ?
Well I'll be! You're already here?
Wow, would you look at that!
Colloquial and friendly. Bah dis donc works too.
Ben dis donc ! Tu as changé de coiffure !
Light surprise, or a hint of disbelief depending on tone.
Eh ben ! Tu as fini tout le gâteau ?
Well! You finished the whole cake?
The modern wow. Also spelled Wouah or Waou.
Wow, that's pretty, I love it!

categories.desc: From mild scolding to setting a boundary.
cards: Mild scolding. Often the start of an indignant rant.
Non mais, t'as vu le prix ?
Come on, did you see the price?
Ça suffit, arrêtez de vous disputer !

categories.desc: Delight, enthusiasm and things going well.
cards: Delight or enthusiasm. A little dated now; génial and super are more common.
Extra ! C'est exactement ce que je voulais.
Terrific! That's exactly what I wanted.
Everything is in order or just right. Said when a job is done well or a plan works.
Childlike joy. Adults use it playfully, or ironically.

categories.desc: Relief after tension, or a narrow escape.
cards: Classic expression of relief or gratitude.
Dieu merci, tout s'est bien passé !
Stronger and more emotional than dieu merci.
Merci mon Dieu ! Tout le monde va bien.
Relief after tension or a narrow escape.
Ouf, j'ai cru qu'on allait le rater !
Phew, I thought we were going to miss it.
Relief that something is over or solved.
Literally ‘we escaped it beautifully’. For avoiding trouble or danger.
On l'a échappé belle ! Un arbre est tombé juste derrière notre voiture.
That was close! A tree fell right behind our car.

categories.desc: Disbelief, distress and things that are appalling.
cards: Mon Dieu, qu'est-ce qui s'est passé ?
The same tone as English ‘OMG’. Very common in speech.
Oh mon Dieu, qu'est-ce que j'ai fait ?
Oh my God, what have I done?
No way! / It can't be true!
Very common for shock or disbelief.
C'est pas vrai ! Il a gagné !
For something tragic, disgusting or appalling.
Amazement or shock, depending on tone.
Incroyable ! Personne ne l'a vu venir.

categories.desc: Playfully old-timey. Fun in writing or when joking around.
cards: Goodness me, I forgot the cake!
Old-fashioned astonishment, now mostly used for comic effect.
